slot.brief: Ice at 0°C (or below 0°C) mixed with water at a given temperature in a calorimeter; do a multi-step heat balance including latent heat and check whether all ice melts before setting the final equilibrium temperature.

stem: A $100$ g piece of ice at $0^\circ$C is mixed with $300$ g of water at $40^\circ$C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. Take $c_{\text{water}}=1\ \text{cal g}^{-1}\, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ and $L_f=80\ \text{cal g}^{-1}$. Find the final temperature.

verdicts.working: Cooling 300 g of water to 0°C releases 300×1×40 = 12,000 cal. Melting the ice takes 100×80 = 8,000 cal, leaving 4,000 cal to warm 400 g of water: ΔT = 4,000/400 = 10°C.

working:
$Q_{\text{water to }0}=300(1)(40)=12000\ \text{cal}$.
$Q_{\text{melt}}=100(80)=8000\ \text{cal}<12000\ \text{cal}$; all ice melts.
$12000=8000+(300+100)(1)T$.
$T=10^\circ\text{C}$

Independent check: Cooling 300 g of water to 0°C releases 300×1×40 = 12,000 cal. Melting the ice takes 100×80 = 8,000 cal, leaving 4,000 cal to warm 400 g of water: ΔT = 4,000/400 = 10°C.
solution:
Heat released by the warm water cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$ is $300(1)(40)=12000\ \text{cal}$, while melting the ice requires $100(80)=8000\ \text{cal}$; hence all the ice melts.
$$12000=8000+(300+100)(1)T \quad\Rightarrow\quad T=10^\circ\text{C}$$

draft.distractor_notes: A: assumes the mixture remains at the melting point. C: uses half the given latent heat. D: ignores the heat required to melt the ice.
